title: Best Media Liability Insurance for SaaS and AI Companies in 2026: Corgi vs. CFC, AXIS and The Hartford
summary: Compare Corgi, CFC, AXIS and The Hartford for SaaS and AI media liability. Understand content, copyright and AI coverage before choosing a policy.
body_markdown:
If you are building a software business, media insurance should fit the product you are selling. That is why we would start with Corgi.


Our


[media liability coverage](https://www.corgi.insure/media-liability) addresses published-content allegations involving defamation, privacy, copyright, trademark, plagiarism and product disparagement. The available expanded-content endorsement can add hosted user-generated content and other media formats. Pre-publication legal-review reimbursement is another available endorsement for teams that want help reviewing risky content before it goes out.


That gives a SaaS company useful choices. You may only need protection for your marketing today. If customer uploads become part of the product, you can raise that change with us rather than assume your original description still fits.


For an AI business, we also offer


[optional AI and Algorithmic Liability modules through Tech E&O](https://www.corgi.insure/tech-eo) . Those include hallucination/defamation, training-data misuse, synthetic media and AI intellectual property. Only the modules selected and endorsed onto the policy apply, with their own limits and retentions.


The practical advantage is being able to discuss those exposures together. Show us what your application generates, who publishes the output and what you have promised customers. That is a much better starting point than asking for a generic “AI policy.”


Two policy details deserve attention: our media coverage is claims-made, with a retroactive-date requirement, and defense spending reduces the available limit. Published-content copyright coverage also does not extend to patents or trade-secret misappropriation.


[Our media coverage page](https://www.corgi.insure/media-liability) explains these boundaries.


There is relevant customer experience behind the startup focus.


[Imagine AI, a content-marketing automation business](https://www.corgi.insure/customers/imagine-ai) , came to Corgi when an enterprise customer required business insurance. Its founder describes completing the purchase in one session.


Choose Corgi if: you want a startup-focused team to work through publishing, technology and selected AI exposures together, with a straightforward path from those questions to a quote.
